title: ABS0990 DO PATIENTS REPORTED OUTCOMES OVERLAP WITH DISEASE ACTIVITY INDICES AND SEVERITY SCORES IN SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS
abstract: Background: Currently, there is equivocal evidence of patients reported outcomes corresponding organ damage in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Evaluating the extent of damage, severity and progression of a disease are crucial aspects. Added to this, an important matter is incorporating the patient's view into the physician's global assessment especially in SSc, where organ damage happens early during the progression of the ailment and which is linked to high disease burden, comorbidities and mortality [1]. Objectives: This study applied the Systemic Sclerosis Impact of Disease questionnaire (ScleroID), Scleroderma Clinical Trials Consortium Damage Index (SCTC-AI), European Scleroderma Study Group activity index (EScSG-AI) and Medsger's Severity Scale (MSS) to an unselected group of patients from an EUSTAR center, analysing the results obtained based on their demographic and clinical characteristics. Moreover, the study aimed to estabilish correlations between patient-reported outcomes measures (PROMs) for SSc and old and new disease activity and severity composite scores. Methods: Our retrospective study included 74 randomly-chosen patients diagnosed with SSc from "Sfanta Maria" Clinical Hospital, Bucharest. All patients were confirmed to meet the ACR-EULAR Classification Criteria for SSc. Furthermore, ethical committee approval was granted for the study and informed consent forms were signed by the patients. For the assessment of the disease activity, SCTC-AI and EScSG-AI were calculated, while the severity of visceral involvement was quantified by MSS. Statistical analyses were performed by Mann-Whitney U test and Spearman's correlation analysis. Results: The cohort included 87.84% women, 12.16% men, 51.35% patients with limited form of the disease, 47.30% with diffuse form and 1.35% sine scleroderma, with a mean age of 57.7±1.25 years and a mean duration of disease of 10.96±1 years. The averages scores were: 4.218±0.250 for ScleroID, 15.65±1.779 for SCTC-AI, 3.878±0.776 for EScSG-AI and 6.581±0.399 for Medsger's scale. ScleroID has positively correlated with SCTC-AI (r=0.398, p=0.0004), EScSG-AI (r=0.373, p=0.001) and MSS (r=0.342, p=0.002). There was no significant difference between gender in mean values of ScleroID (4.25±0.26 vs 3.92±0.73, p=0.504), SCTC-AI (14.97±1.84 vs 20.56±6.18, p=0.336), EScSG-AI (3.98±0.88 vs 3.11±0.71, p=0.591) and MSS (6.58±0.44 vs 6.55±0.85, p=0.815). ScleroID was positively correlate with SCTC-AI (r=0.380, p=0.001), EScSG-AI (r=0.374, p=0.002), and MSS (r=0.339, p=0.005) only in women. In terms of disease duration, this was not correlated with any of the scores: ScleroID (r=0.131, p=0.263), SCTC-AI (r=0.0007, p=0.994), EScSG-AI (r=0.044, p=0.704) and MSS (r=0.186, p=0.11). Patients with diffuse systemic sclerosis had statistically significantly higher values of SCTC-AI (20.31±2.93 vs 11.76±1.93, p=0.015), EScSG-AI (4.28±0.91 vs 3.59±1.26, p=0.003) and MSS (7.94±0.58 vs 5.44±0.48) than patients with limited form, but not for ScleroID questionnaire (4.65±0.36 vs 3.83±0.34, p=0.076). Conclusion: The study demonstrates significant positive correlations between the ScleroID questionnaire and clinical measures of disease activity (SCTC-AI, EScSG-AI) as well as disease severity (MSS). This highlights the relevance of patient-reported outcomes in reflecting clinical disease status in SSc, reinforcing the significance of integrating the patient's perspective in disease evaluation. No correlations were found between disease duration and either clinical or patient-reported outcomes, suggesting an overall high disease burden no matter of disease duration, subtype and visceral involvement. While diffuse SSc is associated with more severe clinical manifestations, the impact on quality of life, as reported by patients, may not always reflect the degree of clinical severity, warranting further research into factors influencing patient perceptions of disease burden. title: Autoantibody reactome analysis reveals diagnostic biomarkers and molecular classification for relapsing polychondritis
abstract: Objectives The lack of effective biomarkers for relapsing polychondritis (RP) poses a significant challenge in its early diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to identify novel autoantibodies and elucidate the pathogenesis and molecular heterogeneity of RP. Methods Plasma samples from 467 RP patients, 164 healthy controls (HCs), and 186 disease controls (DCs) were analysed using 2 sequential microarrays and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay to sequentially discover, validate, and verify new autoantibodies. Machine learning and differential analysis were used to identify diagnosis-specific autoantibodies and their correlation with disease activity, recurrence, and remission. Results The RP group had 1344 elevated autoantibodies, discriminating RP patients from HCs. These antigenic targets were associated with pathways involving autoimmune responses, infections, and cardiovascular lesions. Two molecular subtypes characterised by distinct organ involvement and prognosis highlighted the heterogeneity of RP. Notably, 14 new autoantibodies were identified, which differentiated RP versus HCs and DCs with a sensitivity of 41% and 49.7% and a specificity of 91.7% and 90.5%, respectively. Among them, 6 autoantibodies showed better diagnostic performance and were consistently verified. Specifically, anti-C4B was positively correlated with disease activity, and increased anti-KRT16 predicted RP recurrence within 1 year. In addition, anti-C4B, anti-FNBP4, and anti-KRT10 decreased from acute attack to remission. Furthermore, the deposition of C4B protein in tracheal tissues, coupled with its reduction in plasma of RP patients, indicated that abnormal complement activation might be related to the pathological mechanism of RP. Conclusions The 14 autoantibodies promoted a noninvasive early detection of RP, predicted disease recurrence and provided new insights into the understanding of RP pathogenesis.
